title: Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

reading.body:
This is a deception carried out at the display layer of a financial interface. The screen the victim checked to see whether his money was growing was controlled by the people taking it, and it asserted false account information as fact. The app was made to look like a legitimate trading platform, so the impersonation was of a trusted service rather than of a person, and the false balances were the product being sold.

The failure sits at the point where a user verifies his own position. Small trades and modest withdrawals were permitted early, which made the interface's claims look consistent with reality, and the false information appeared only inside a system the scammers operated. Nothing inside that system could contradict it. Catching it would have required confirmation from a source outside the interface, such as the venue actually holding the funds, and the reports do not describe any such check being available to the couple.

What is not established is that anyone has been charged or that any of the money has been recovered. The reports describe a police account of a fake AI-generated website, and they do not say which parts of it were generated by AI or how.

reports.title: Georgia couple loses $800K in sophisticated cryptocurrency scam
Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

summary:
A retired Georgia couple lost nearly $800,000 in a sophisticated cryptocurrency scam that started with a WhatsApp message from a stranger. The scammer convinced Jerry Dunaway to invest through a legitimate-looking mobile trading app, initially allowing him to make small trades and withdraw modest amounts to build trust. However, police later discovered that scammers had created a fake AI-generated website that displayed false investment information on the screen, tricking Dunaway into believing his money was growing.

When Dunaway attempted to withdraw a larger amount last week, he discovered the funds were gone and called 911. The couple, Jerry and Mindy Dunaway, are now speaking publicly to warn others about the sophisticated tactics used by scammers. Police indicate that victims in these cases rarely recover their money. The couple's children have created a GoFundMe page to help them cover daily expenses as they work with Gwinnett County investigators.
